readback.name: Poincare.stereoInvFunAuxConformalFactor
readback.mathematical_statement: This is data, not a proposition. For every normed additive commutative group E in any universe u_1, it defines a real-valued function lambda(z) = 16/(||z||^2+4)^2. The exponents are natural-number squares and the operations and quotient are in R. No real-vector-space, inner-product, finite-dimensionality, completeness, sphere, unit-vector, orthogonality, or measurable-structure hypothesis is required by this definition. The denominator is positive for every z, so the formula is globally defined and gives the squared length-scaling factor used later; lambda(0)=1. Those facts explain the definition, while this frozen declaration itself is a function type and asserts no derivative or metric theorem. E alone carries the universe parameter u_1 and the output R is in universe zero. In the subsequent unit-sphere application the constant 4 comes from Mathlib's scaled stereographic coordinates and does not change the sphere radius from one.

readback.name: Poincare.stereoInvFunAuxFDeriv
readback.mathematical_statement: This is a definition of a continuous R-linear endomorphism, not a proposition. Let E be any real inner-product space with its compatible normed additive commutative group structure, in any universe u_1. For arbitrary v,z in E set a = (||z||^2+4)^(-1). It defines L(v,z) = (4*a) I - (8*a^2)(u maps to <z,u>_R z) + (16*a^2)(u maps to <z,u>_R v), where I is the continuous R-linear identity on E. The rank-one operators are the innerSL R z functional followed by scalar multiplication of z and v, respectively. The result has type E ->L[R] E and uses the real identity ring homomorphism. The parameter z is the intended derivative point and v is a fixed pole parameter, but this definition alone asserts no derivative relationship. There is no assumption that v is unit, that z or the input direction is orthogonal to v, or that E is finite-dimensional or complete. The fields are specifically real and E is universe-polymorphic; no complex-inner-product version is quantified.

readback.name: Poincare.stereoInvFunAuxFDeriv_apply
readback.mathematical_statement: For every real inner-product space E with compatible normed additive commutative group structure in any universe u_1 and arbitrary v,z,u in E, put a = (||z||^2+4)^(-1). The defined continuous R-linear map satisfies L(v,z)(u) = (4*a) u - (8*a^2*<z,u>_R) z + (16*a^2*<z,u>_R) v. Every coefficient and inner product is real. This expands the operator definition on a direction u, and places no unit-length or orthogonality restriction on any vector. There is no finite-dimensionality, completeness, nonzero-vector, sphere-valuedness, or manifold hypothesis. It does not itself assert that L is a derivative; the following HasFDerivAt declaration supplies that assertion. The ambient E may have any dimension, including zero or infinite dimension, and its single universe parameter is u_1.

readback.name: Poincare.hasFDerivAt_stereoInvFunAuxFDeriv
readback.mathematical_statement: In any real inner-product space E with compatible normed additive commutative group structure and arbitrary universe u_1, for all fixed v and all z in E, the full ambient map F_v(w) = (||w||^2+4)^(-1) times [4 w + (||w||^2-4) v], with real scalar multiplication, has real Frechet derivative L(v,z) at z. Explicitly, with a=(||z||^2+4)^(-1), this derivative sends u to 4*a u - 8*a^2*<z,u>_R z + 16*a^2*<z,u>_R v. HasFDerivAt concerns the ordinary full neighborhood filter at z in E, not differentiation within a sphere or hyperplane. The denominator is strictly positive everywhere, so no excluded point condition is necessary. v and z are unrestricted; v need not have norm one and z need not be orthogonal to v. Consequently this is a theorem about the globally defined auxiliary map E->E, which need not have sphere-valued output for such unrestricted parameters. It assumes neither finite-dimensionality nor completeness, and makes no metric-conformality or Poincare-conjecture claim. R is the differentiation field in universe zero; E is in arbitrary universe u_1.

readback.name: Poincare.fderiv_stereoInvFunAux
readback.mathematical_statement: For any real inner-product space E with compatible normed additive commutative group structure in any universe u_1 and all v,z in E, the real Frechet derivative fderiv R (stereoInvFunAux v) z equals the continuous R-linear endomorphism L(v,z). Here stereoInvFunAux v is exactly F_v(w)=(||w||^2+4)^(-1) times [4 w+(||w||^2-4) v], and L(v,z)(u)=4*a u-8*a^2*<z,u>_R z+16*a^2*<z,u>_R v with a=(||z||^2+4)^(-1). The equality is in E->L[R] E, for the derivative of the full ambient map at an arbitrary point. It has no unit-length, orthogonality, finite-dimensionality, completeness, sphere, or manifold assumption. The preceding HasFDerivAt statement gives actual differentiability everywhere, so the fderiv here represents that actual derivative. The theorem does not assert a derivative with values in a tangent-space subtype, conformality without further hypotheses, or a global topological result.

readback.name: Poincare.fderiv_stereoInvFunAux_comp_subtype
readback.mathematical_statement: For any real inner-product space E with compatible normed additive commutative group structure in any universe u_1 and any v in E, let H=(span_R {v})^perp, the orthogonal-complement submodule, equipped with its inherited norm and real inner product. For every z in the subtype H, the real Frechet derivative of the map H->E taking h to stereoInvFunAux v (h:E) equals L(v,(z:E)) composed with the continuous R-linear inclusion H.subtypeL:H->L[R] E. Thus its value on u in H is the ambient formula 4*a (u:E)-8*a^2*<(z:E),(u:E)>_R (z:E)+16*a^2*<(z:E),(u:E)>_R v, where a=(||(z:E)||^2+4)^(-1). Orthogonality of z and directions is encoded by the domain subtype, while v is unrestricted and need not be unit or nonzero. This is the ordinary derivative in the normed space H, with codomain the ambient E. It assumes no finite-dimensionality or completeness and does not make the codomain a sphere or sphere tangent space. In particular the statement is meaningful for v=0, when H=E. It is a derivative-composition identity, with no conformal metric or chart-homeomorphism conclusion.

readback.name: Poincare.inner_stereoInvFunAuxFDeriv_of_mem_orthogonal
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E be any real inner-product space with compatible normed additive commutative group structure in any universe u_1. For v,z,u,w in E assume ||v||=1 and assume separately that z,u,w all belong to H=(span_R {v})^perp, equivalently that their real inner products with v vanish. Then <L(v,z)u,L(v,z)w>_R = [16/(||z||^2+4)^2] * <u,w>_R. The right-hand coefficient is exactly the pinned stereoInvFunAuxConformalFactor, a squared length factor. The conclusion concerns the ambient inner product of the derivative images of the two permitted directions, and both inner products are real. All three orthogonality hypotheses matter: z locates the inverse stereographic chart in H, and u,w are its directions in H. Unit length of v fixes the sphere radius to one. Under these assumptions the underlying auxiliary map F_v on H is the inverse of Mathlib's stereographic chart of the unit sphere centered at zero with pole v removed, with forward normalization 2/(1-<v,x>_R) times orthogonal projection. F_v(0)=-v, its derivative at zero on H is the inclusion, and this coefficient equals one at zero. No dimension is fixed and no finite-dimensionality or completeness is required. This frozen conclusion is a pointwise inner-product scaling identity; it does not construct a global metric, prove a chart change, or assert this formula for directions outside H. In the pinned round-three-sphere context the ambient space is R^4 and H is three-dimensional, but that is a specialization of this general real theorem. There is no orientation or measure assumption and no Poincare-conjecture claim.

readback.name: Poincare.inner_fderiv_stereoInvFunAux_comp_subtype
readback.mathematical_statement: For any real inner-product space E with compatible normed additive commutative group structure in any universe u_1, take v in E with ||v||=1 and put H=(span_R {v})^perp. For every base point z and directions u,w in the normed real subspace H, let A_z be the real Frechet derivative at z of H->E given by h maps to stereoInvFunAux v (h:E). Then <A_z u,A_z w>_R = [16/(||(z:E)||^2+4)^2] * <u,w>_R. The left-hand inner product is in the ambient E; the right-hand inner product is the inherited inner product on H, equal to the ambient pairing of its underlying vectors. Orthogonality of all three vectors is carried by their subtype membership; only the unit-length condition on v is a separate premise. The coefficient is the exact pinned conformal factor of Mathlib's unit-sphere inverse stereographic normalization, whose ambient formula is (||h||^2+4)^(-1) times [4 h+(||h||^2-4) v] and whose value at h=0 is -v. The square-root length factor is 4/(||h||^2+4), so the squared metric factor is 16/(||h||^2+4)^2 and equals one at zero. The map is differentiated as an H->E map; the conclusion does not itself identify a sphere tangent space or a chosen R^n coordinate chart. E need not be finite-dimensional or complete and no dimension is fixed. The pinned RoundSphere3 is the radius-one sphere in EuclideanSpace R (Fin 4), with the ambient-inner-product pullback metric and a three-dimensional model; applying this theorem there preserves that radius-one normalization. There are no orientation, measure, compactness, or manifold assumptions in this exact frozen type. It asserts pointwise conformality of the derivative on H, not a global Poincare or constant-curvature theorem.
